01
Home / Architecture Flow

Architecture Flow

How a quiz answer travels through the system: from the student's screen, through the safety checks and AI agents, into the database and back.

Contents 1Overview 2The learner loop 3Four-tier architecture 4Life of a request 5Inside the AI engine 6Trust boundaries 7Runtime & deployment 8Dependencies

1Overview

Concept Bridge is two small Python programs that run side by side. Gradio draws the screens. Flask does all the real work: sign-in, grading, saving and calling the AI. The AI never grades, never saves and never decides who can do what. It only explains.

What the student sees

A quiz, an instant score, a list of “why you got it wrong” gaps and a lesson for each one.

What the server decides

Which questions to ask, whether answers are right, who owns what, and what gets saved.

What the AI adds

The likely misconception, the missing prerequisite, the lesson, the analogy and new check questions.

2The learner loop

Six steps. Green steps use AI; the rest is plain code, so they behave the same way every time.

Learner loop flowchart
StepWho does itWhat happens
1 · Pick a subjectStudentChooses .NET (taught in C#) or Java.
2 · Take the quizFlaskPicks 5 questions, one for each concept, from the 20-question bank. Answer keys never leave the server.
3 · ScoreFlaskCompares each choice with the stored key. Each quiz can be submitted once.
4 · DiagnoseMisconceptionAnalyst agentFor each wrong answer, names the likely misconception and picks the missing prerequisite from an allowed list.
5 · TeachMicroLessonDesigner agentWrites a short explanation, a real-world analogy, a worked example and next steps.
6 · CheckFlaskScores the 2 new questions the lesson created. Answers stay on the server until submitted.

3Four-tier architecture

Each tier only talks to the one next to it. That keeps the AI far away from passwords, scores and the database.

System architecture component diagram

1 · UI

Gradio web app for quizzes, lessons, progress and the Teaching Studio. Holds no secrets beyond the user's own session.

2 · API & safety

Flask with Waitress. Sign-in, roles, CSRF, rate limits, grading, saving, and the input/output guardrails.

3 · AI engine

Microsoft Agent Framework agents using the OpenAI SDK, with one read-only tool and a separate reviewer.

4 · Data

SQLite for accounts, quizzes, lessons, drafts and the audit log. JSON files for questions and concepts.

4Life of a request: “Analyze my gaps”

This is the most important path in the app. Notice how many checks happen before anything the AI wrote is saved.

POST /api/attempts/{id}/analyze sequence diagram
Saved once. A second call returns the stored diagnosis instead of paying for a new one.
Answers can't change. If the answers sent differ from the graded ones, the request is refused (409).
Fails closed. If any check fails, nothing is saved and the student is asked to retry.

5Inside the AI engine

Every AI task runs the same bounded pipeline. Application code, not the agent, decides the order of steps.

Agent pipeline flowchart
AgentJobTool accessOutput contract
MisconceptionAnalystOne gap per wrong answer, with evidenceconcept_catalog, only the allowed conceptsDiagnosis
MicroLessonDesignerExplanation, analogy, example, steps, 2 new checksconcept_catalog, only the gap's conceptsLesson
QuestionAuthorOne new multiple-choice draft for teacher reviewconcept_catalog, one conceptDraftQuestion
SafetyAndPedagogyReviewerApproves or rejects every output aboveNoneApprove / reject
Max 3 stepsMax 4 tool calls35 s per agent run90 s per task0 retriesUnknown tool → stopConfidence ≤ 0.85

6Trust boundaries

Code and server settings are trusted. Anything typed by a student or written by the model is treated as data, never as an instruction.

Trusted and untrusted zones boundary diagram

Trusted Code & server

  • Source code and the JSON question/concept banks
  • Server settings and the API key in backend/.env
  • Session identity and role from SQLite
  • Teacher/admin accounts made by the operator
vs

Untrusted Inputs & AI output

  • Optional learner reasoning and any JSON a client sends
  • Every diagnosis, lesson and draft the model writes
  • Optional web-search excerpts (off by default)
  • Anything in the Gradio page state

OpenAI call settings

store=False

Asks the provider not to store responses.

35 s timeout

Per SDK request; 90 s total per AI task.

0 retries

A failure stops cleanly. Scores are already saved.

Request IDs

Users see an ID, never provider errors or secrets.

7Runtime & deployment

python run.py starts both programs and stops both on Ctrl+C. Everything listens on this computer only.

Runtime view deployment diagram

A1Architecture overview

Five layers. Read top to bottom: people use the Gradio app, Flask runs every step and owns every decision, guardrails sit on each boundary, the agents only suggest, and the data layer holds the facts.

LayerWhat it holdsJob
InterfaceGradio app, operator CLIShows quizzes, scores, gaps and lessons; staff accounts are made locally
CoreFlask API on WaitressRuns every step in a fixed order; grades, authorizes and saves
GuardrailsInput screen, schemas, output validationStops unsafe text going in and unsafe output coming out
AI engine3 worker agents, 1 reviewer, 1 read-only toolExplains mistakes and drafts teaching content
DataSQLite, JSON banks, translationsThe only source of facts, answers and history
The central rule: code decides, AI suggests. No score, role, answer key or saved record ever depends on what the model says.

B7Key algorithms

01

Quiz selection

  1. Pool = bank questions for the subject + teacher-approved drafts.
  2. Count each concept's past misses for this student.
  3. Shuffle concepts, then sort by misses (most first).
  4. Take 5 concepts and pick one random question each.
02

Grading

  1. Exactly 5 answers, one per question, choice 0–3.
  2. Compare with the server-side key; score out of 5.
  3. Reasoning is screened, then stripped before saving.
  4. Saved only if not already graded (409 otherwise).
03

Diagnosis validation

  1. All correct → summary, no AI call.
  2. Allowed list = each wrong concept + its prerequisites.
  3. One gap per wrong answer, same concept, allowed prerequisite.
  4. Confidence ≤ 0.85; saved once.
04

Input screening

  1. NFKC normalize; strip invisible format characters.
  2. Decode base64-looking tokens that hold readable text.
  3. Check original + decoded text against injection rules.
  4. Reject emails, phone/card numbers and keys.
05

Bounded agent run

  1. Max 3 steps, 4 tool calls, 35 s; unknown tools end the run.
  2. Input wrapped as untrusted_task_data.
  3. Structured output → strict schema → output check.
  4. Reviewer must approve; 90 s total per task.
06

Mastery scoring

  1. Exactly 2 answers, choice 0–3.
  2. Compared with keys kept on the server.
  3. Mastered only when both are right.
  4. Scored once; a new lesson gives new checks.

C · Architecture decision recordsAll 8 ADRs from docs/ADR.md, all accepted

C1Decision map

Which decision shapes which part of the system.

C2The 8 decisions

ADR-001

Separate Python Gradio app

Accepted
ContextA separate JavaScript stack adds tooling and attack surface.
→
DecisionGradio UI in Python, Flask middle tier, own database.
→
OutcomeOne language end to end; no Node.js needed.
ADR-002

Teach .NET through C#

Accepted
Context.NET is a platform, not a language.
→
DecisionLabelled C# snippets for .NET; a parallel Java track.
→
OutcomeLanguage-correct beginner tracks for both subjects.
ADR-003

Bounded agents, deterministic authority

Accepted
ContextAgents with broad power can be talked into acting.
→
DecisionScoped read-only tool; reviewer without tools; code owns scores and writes.
→
OutcomeUseful reasoning with tightly limited authority.
ADR-004

Strict outputs + business checks

Accepted
ContextA schema alone can't prove an answer is right.
→
DecisionStrict schemas plus graph, coverage, privacy, confidence and reviewer checks.
→
OutcomeInvalid output fails closed and is never saved.
ADR-005

SQLite and local roles

Accepted
ContextA classroom app shouldn't need a database server.
→
DecisionLocal SQLite (foreign keys, WAL); staff via CLI; hashed sessions.
→
OutcomeZero-setup deployment with real role separation.
ADR-006

Human approval to publish

Accepted
ContextNew questions become lasting content.
→
DecisionDrafts stay pending until a teacher confirms with confirmed:true.
→
OutcomeA human gate on everything that enters quizzes.
ADR-007

Honest evaluation evidence

Accepted
ContextAI quality must be shown, not claimed.
→
DecisionOffline, mocked and live results kept separate; failures stay in totals.
→
OutcomeEvery number comes from a real, repeatable run.
ADR-008

Minimize learner data

Accepted
ContextStudent data is sensitive.
→
DecisionNicknames only; raw reasoning not stored; analytics and sharing off; no uploads.
→
OutcomePrivacy by default for every learner.

6Quality hardening

Improvements made during the final QA pass, each confirmed by the full test suite.

Multilingual injection defense

Detects override attempts in English, Spanish and Hindi, chat-tag and tag-breakout tricks, hidden characters and base64-encoded instructions. 20 of 20 attack probes blocked.

Zero false alarms

Separate input and output policies, so real coding talk like java Main, 2147483647 or “delete from an array” works. 7/7 explanations and 4/4 lessons pass.

108/108 tests green

Full suite passing with 85% coverage, verified 3 times including from a fresh unzip.

Clean multilingual text

UTF-8 throughout, so dashes and symbols display correctly in every language and in the CLI.

Consistent code style

ruff check and ruff format clean across the project; docs match the measured results.

Lean, secret-free package

A 41 MB source-only build with a placeholder .env: no database, caches or keys inside.

Change→ruff→pytest 108/108→offline eval 31/31→re-verified from the clean package
Live AI quality run is built in. The 20-case golden dataset and LLM judge run with one command in the deployment environment (see Evaluation).

Home / Responsible AI

Responsible AI

How the project uses AI wisely: every item from the guidelines file, the control that meets it, and proof that it works.

Contents 1Principles 2Defense in depth 3Four shields 4Guidelines map 5Try the guardrails 6Human in the loop 7Privacy & transparency 8Evaluation & judge

1Principles

AI advises, code decides

Scores, roles and saves never depend on the model.

Least privilege

One read-only tool, limited to the concepts a task needs.

Humans own lasting content

Teachers approve every new question.

Honest & traceable

AI output is labelled; every step is audited without content.

2Defense in depth

Each layer assumes the one before it might fail.

Safety layers on one AI request flowchart

3Four shields: model, agent, tool, app

The guidelines ask for guardrails at the model, agent, tool and application levels. They nest like this, so a request passes every shield in turn.

Four nested shields how one request passes them
1

Model

  • Learner text wrapped as untrusted data
  • Strict Pydantic schemas
  • Confidence capped at 0.85
  • store=False
2

Agent

  • Reviewer must approve
  • Max 3 steps, 4 tool calls, 35 s
  • Unknown tool call ends the run
  • No keys, accounts or writes
3

Tool

  • Only concept_catalog, read-only
  • Locked to allowed IDs
  • Out-of-scope reads denied & logged
  • Web search off by default
4

Application

  • Student / teacher / admin roles
  • Teacher approval to publish
  • Deterministic grading
  • Content-free audit log

3Student guide

Student journey user flow

Step by step

1Sign up with a nickname and a 12–128 character password.
2Choose English, Hindi, Tamil or Spanish.
3Pick .NET or Java and start a 5-question quiz.
4Answer each question. Optionally explain your thinking, or use voice and read-aloud.
5Submit for your score, then choose Analyze conceptual gaps.
6Open a lesson for a gap: explanation, analogy, worked example.
7Answer the 2 mastery checks. Review everything in My progress.

Tips

  • Your reasoning helps the diagnosis but is not stored.
  • Don't type emails, phone numbers or keys; they are refused.
  • Each quiz and each mastery check can be submitted once.
  • AI help is limited to 10 diagnoses and 10 lessons per hour.
  • After reloading the page, sign in again (by design).

4Teacher & admin guide

Teacher journey user flow
Who can do what role map

Teaching Studio

1Sign in with the account the operator created.
2Select Refresh to see concept trends across quizzes and checks.
3Generate an AI question draft for a concept.
4Read the question, options, answer and explanation. Edit if needed.
5Approve or reject, then confirm. Only approved drafts enter quizzes.
6Admins can also open the audit log.

7Security checklist (OWASP)

01Access control: role, owner and state checksPass
02Hashed passwords and sessions, 1-hour expiryPass
03CSRF token on every write; other origins refusedPass
04Parameterized SQL; no code is ever runPass
05Strict schemas, 20 KB cap, rate limitsPass
06Public sign-up is student onlyPass
07Headers: no-store, nosniff, DENY, no-referrerPass
08No stack traces or provider errors shownPass
09Content-free audit of auth, guardrail, agent eventsPass
10Pinned packages; pip-audit finds no known issuesPass

8Troubleshooting

Find the fix from the message decision tree
“Configure OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL…”

Add both to backend/.env and restart. Quizzes and scoring work without them.

Health says AI is configured, but calls fail

/api/health only checks that settings exist. Check the model name and the base URL.

“Please explain the topic without instructions to the AI…”

The reasoning box looked like an instruction to the AI. Rephrase it as your own explanation.

“Please remove personal information or credentials…”

Remove emails, phone or card numbers, and keys from the text.

“Diagnosis did not match the prerequisite graph. Please retry.”

The AI suggested something outside the allowed concepts, so it was refused. Retry; your score is safe.

Signed out after reloading

By design, the UI keeps your session only for the open page.

Too many requests

Rate limits protect cost: 15 quizzes, 10 diagnoses and 10 lessons per hour.
